l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The house of Israel is compared to an olive-tree whose branches are broken off and scattered over the earth. After the Gentiles receive the fulness of the Gospel, its natural branches are grafted in again.

l: the twelve apostles of the Lamb, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The twelve apostles of the Lamb follow the Lamb and are opposed by the multitude of the earth. They shall judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

l: twelve ministers of Nephi's seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The twelve ministers of Nephi’s seed are chosen and ordained of God to minister to his seed. They shall judge Nephi’s seed and are made righteous through faith in the Lamb of God.

l: seed of Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Nephi’s seed experiences wars and contentions, gathers against the seed of his brethren, and is overcome because of its pride and the temptations of the devil. The people of Nephi’s seed are eventually overpowered and many generations pass away.

l: the seed of Nephi's brethren, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The seed of Nephi’s brethren contends against Nephi’s seed and overpowers it. It later goes forth in multitudes, experiences wars, dwindles in unbelief, and becomes dark, loathsome, filthy, idle, and full of abominations.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Jerusalem is described as a great city that will be destroyed and whose people will be carried captive into Babylon. After the captivity, the Jews will return and possess the land of their inheritance.

l: Nazareth, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Nazareth is the city where Nephi sees a virgin who is exceedingly fair and white.

l: land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The land of promise is shown to Nephi as the setting for multitudes, wars, generations, judgments, and the coming of the Lamb of God. Cities sink or burn, mountains and plains are broken, and the earth experiences earthquakes and great tumult.

l: the tree of life, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The tree of life is shown to Nephi as beautiful and white beyond comparison. It represents the love of God and is connected with the fountain of living waters.

l: the fruit of the tree, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The fruit of the tree is the fruit that Lehi tasted, and Nephi is shown the tree that bore it. The tree and its fruit are associated with the love of God, which is most desirable and joyous to the soul.

l: love of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The love of God is represented by the tree of life and the waters of the fountain of living waters. It sheds itself abroad in the hearts of the children of men and is desirable above all things and joyous to the soul.

l: the rod of iron, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The rod of iron represents the word of God. It leads to the fountain of living waters, or to the tree of life.

l: the river of water, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The fountain of filthy water, or the river seen by Lehi, represents the depths of hell.

l: the great and spacious building, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The large and spacious building represents the pride of the world and the vain imaginations and pride of the children of men. It falls, and its fall is exceedingly great.

l: the mist of darkness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The mists of darkness represent the temptations of the devil. They blind the eyes, harden the hearts of the children of men, and lead them onto broad roads where they perish and are lost.

l: the gospel of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The gospel is preached among the Jews, and its fulness is received by the Gentiles. After this, the natural branches of the house of Israel are grafted in and come to know the true Messiah.

l: faith, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Faith in the Son of God allows Nephi to receive revelation by the power of the Holy Ghost. Faith in the Lamb of God makes the garments of the twelve ministers white in his blood.

l: sin, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Lamb of God takes away the sins of the world. Those who are in a lost and fallen state must rely on the Redeemer.

l: judgment, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Every person will be brought into judgment. Those who have sought to do wickedly are unclean before the judgment-seat of God and cannot dwell with God.

l: baptism of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The prophet prepares the way for the Messiah and baptizes him with water. After the baptism, the heavens open and the Holy Ghost comes down in the form of a dove.

l: crucifixion of Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Lamb of God is taken by the people, judged by the world, lifted up upon the cross, and slain for the sins of the world.

l: resurrection of Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: After the Messiah is slain, he rises from the dead and makes himself manifest by the Holy Ghost unto the Gentiles.

l: the scattering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The house of Israel is scattered over all the face of the earth, and its branches are compared to branches broken off from an olive-tree.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: After the house of Israel is scattered, it is gathered together again. The remnants of the house of Israel are grafted in and come to the knowledge of the true Messiah.

l: wars among Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Nephi sees multitudes of his people gathered to battle, with wars, rumors of wars, great slaughters, and many generations passing away in wars and contentions.

l: destruction of the land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The land of promise suffers great judgments, including darkness, lightnings, thunderings, earthquakes, broken rocks and plains, sinking cities, burning cities, and tumbling mountains.

l: pride of the world, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The large and spacious building represents the pride of the world. It falls with an exceedingly great fall.

l: temptations of the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The temptations of the devil are represented by the mists of darkness. They blind eyes, harden hearts, and lead people away into broad roads where they perish and are lost.

l: the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The devil tempts the children of men, blinds their eyes, hardens their hearts, and leads them away into broad roads that cause them to perish and be lost.

l: unbelief, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Jews dwindle in unbelief, and the seed of Nephi’s brethren also dwindles in unbelief. That seed becomes dark, loathsome, filthy, idle, and full of abominations.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: Nephi sees the nations and kingdoms of the Gentiles, the formation and works of the great and abominable church, and the scattering and suffering of the seed of his brethren. He learns that the book of the Lamb of God came from the Jews, that plain and precious parts of the gospel and covenants were taken away, and that further records will restore them. The Gentiles may be numbered among the house of Israel if they hearken to the Lamb of God and repent, while the church of the Lamb and the covenant people are armed with righteousness against the great abominable church. Nephi is shown that John, one of the twelve apostles of the Lamb, will write the remainder of the vision concerning the end of the world.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: Nephi sees many nations and kingdoms, the Gentiles, the great and abominable church, the book of the Lamb of God, and events concerning the house of Israel. He hears that John will write the remainder of the things shown, and he ends his record of this vision while bearing record that what he has written is true.

l: John, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: John is identified as one of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. He will see and write the remainder of the things shown, including things concerning the end of the world.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: God is identified as the founder of the covenants with the house of Israel and as the source of power, judgment, mercy, and salvation described in the vision. He will manifest himself unto all nations.

l: the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The Lamb of God is the Son of the Eternal Father and the Savior of the world. He will bring forth much of his gospel, manifest himself unto the Gentiles and the Jews, and establish his words through the records of Nephi's seed and the twelve apostles.

l: the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The devil is shown as the founder of the great and abominable church. He seeks to lead away the souls of men into captivity, destruction, and hell.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The Gentiles form nations and kingdoms, receive the book of the Lamb of God, and obtain the promised land. If they hearken to the Lamb of God and do not harden their hearts, they may be numbered among the seed of Nephi's father and the house of Israel; if they repent not, they must perish.

l: the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The Jews are the source from whose mouth the book of the Lamb of God proceeds. The book first goes forth from the Jews in purity through the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The house of Israel receives the covenants of the Lord and is visited in judgment and mercy. Gentiles who hearken to the Lamb of God may be numbered among the house of Israel, and the work of the Father will prepare the way for the fulfillment of its covenants.

l: remnant of the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The seed of Nephi's father is visited in judgment, smitten by the hand of the Gentiles, and later receives further records. Gentiles who hearken to the Lamb of God may be numbered among this seed.

l: the seed of Nephi's brethren, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The seed of Nephi's brethren is separated from the Gentiles by many waters, scattered, smitten, and subjected to the wrath of God. The Lord will not suffer the Gentiles to utterly destroy it, and the book of the Lamb of God and other records will come unto its remnant.

l: the great and abominable church, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The great and abominable church is founded by the devil and slays, tortures, binds, and brings the saints of God into captivity. It takes away plain and precious parts of the gospel and many covenants, and it gathers multitudes to fight against the Lamb of God.

l: the church of the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The church of the Lamb of God consists of the saints of God and is found across the earth, though its numbers and dominions are few because of the wickedness of the great whore. Its members receive the power of the Lamb and are armed with righteousness and the power of God.

l: the twelve apostles of the Lamb, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The twelve apostles of the Lamb bear record of the truth in the Lamb of God and carry the book from the Jews unto the Gentiles. Their record will be established with the records of Nephi's seed.

l: the promised land, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The promised land is the land of inheritance covenanted by the Lord God to the seed of Nephi's father. The Gentiles who go forth out of captivity prosper and obtain it, and those who hearken to the Lamb may be blessed upon it forever.

l: the book of the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The book of the Lamb of God is a record of the Jews containing the covenants of the Lord, many prophecies, and the fulness of the gospel when it first proceeds from the Jews. Plain and precious things are taken from it, but later records establish its truth and make those things known.

l: the gospel of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The gospel of the Lamb goes forth from the Jews in purity, but the great and abominable church takes away many plain and precious parts. The Lamb will bring forth much of it in plain and precious form, including his rock and salvation.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The covenants of the Lord are contained in the book of the Lamb of God and concern the house of Israel. The great and abominable church takes away many covenants, but the Lord will fulfill them and make them known.

l: the marvelous work among the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The great and marvelous work will be worked among the children of men. It will lead either to their convincing unto peace and life eternal or to the hardness of their hearts, blindness of their minds, captivity, and destruction.

l: captivity, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The Gentiles go forth out of captivity upon the many waters and are delivered by the power of God from other nations. The devil seeks to bring souls into captivity, while those who hearken to the Lamb will be no more brought down into captivity.

l: wars among the nations, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: Wars and rumors of wars arise among all the nations belonging to the mother of abominations. These events occur as the wrath of God is poured out upon the great and abominable church.

l: the wrath of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The wrath of God is upon the seed of Nephi's brethren, who are scattered and smitten before the Gentiles. It is also poured out upon those gathered against the Gentiles and upon the great and abominable church.

l: repentance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 13 .. Chapter 14
s: The Gentiles are told that if they repent it will be well with them. Those who repent not must perish, while those who hearken to the Lamb and do not harden their hearts may become part of the house of Israel.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi explains to his brethren the meanings of his father's dream, including the tree of life, the rod of iron, the river of water, the separation of the wicked and righteous, and the future restoration and grafting in of the remnant of Israel. The Lord commands Nephi's father to lead the family into the wilderness, where the ball guides their journey and provides written directions according to their faith and diligence. After Nephi's bow breaks, the family suffers famine and murmurs against the Lord, but Nephi makes a new bow, obtains food, and the family is blessed. Ishmael dies at Nahom, after which the daughters of Ishmael and others murmur and seek to return to Jerusalem, but the Lord chastens them and provides food again.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi returns to his father's tent, explains his father's teachings and dream to his brethren, and exhorts them to keep the commandments of the Lord. After his steel bow breaks, he makes a wooden bow, follows the ball's directions, obtains food, and returns with joy to his family.

l: Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Ishmael travels with Nephi's family in the wilderness and dies at Nahom.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The Messiah is to be manifested in body to the children of men, after which the fulness of the gospel of the Messiah will come to the Gentiles and then to the remnant of the seed.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The Lord makes knowledge available to those who ask in faith and keep his commandments. He commands Nephi's father to journey into the wilderness, chastens him and others for murmuring, and blesses the family with food.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi's father receives revelations concerning the journey into the wilderness and the ball. He murmurs during the famine, is chastened by the Lord, and inquires of the Lord after Nephi's exhortation.

l: Laman and Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The brethren dispute over their father's words, fail to inquire of the Lord, and are rebuked by Nephi. They later humble themselves, follow the ball, suffer from the famine, and are chastened for their anger and murmuring.

l: the daughters of Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The daughters of Ishmael travel in the wilderness and mourn exceedingly after Ishmael's death. They murmur against Nephi's father and Nephi and desire to return to Jerusalem.

l: the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The Jews are to reject the Lord, be scattered by the Gentiles, and later be restored in the latter days so that they will not be confounded or scattered again.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The Gentiles are the means through which the natural branches are grafted in and through which the Lord shows his power after being rejected by the Jews.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The house of Israel is compared to an olive-tree, and its people are scattered and later remembered and restored according to the covenant made with Abraham.

l: the remnant of our seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The remnant of the seed will dwindle in unbelief for many years, then receive the fulness of the gospel through the Gentiles, recognize their place in the house of Israel, and come to know their Redeemer.

l: the wicked, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The wicked are separated from the righteous and from the tree of life by the justice of God. If they die in their wickedness, they cannot dwell in the kingdom of God and are cast into hell.

l: the righteous, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The righteous are justified by the truth and will be lifted up at the last day. They are separated from the wicked by the justice of God.

l: the valley of Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The valley of Lemuel is where Nephi's father dwells in a tent while the events concerning the marriages and the command to journey into the wilderness occur.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The wilderness is the destination of Nephi's family after leaving their former land. They travel through it for many days, suffer hunger, follow the ball, and obtain food by hunting.

l: the kingdom of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The kingdom of God is clean, and no unclean thing can enter it. The wicked cannot dwell there if their works are filthy.

l: hell, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Hell is prepared for the wicked and is the place to which those rejected from the righteous and the tree of life are cast.

l: the tree of life, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The tree of life represents the tree seen in Nephi's father's dream. Its fruit is most precious and desirable above all other fruits and is the greatest of the gifts of God.

l: the olive-tree, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The olive-tree represents the house of Israel. Natural branches are broken off and later grafted into the true olive-tree.

l: the natural branches, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The natural branches represent the remnant of Israel. They are scattered by the Gentiles and are later grafted into the true olive-tree.

l: the rod of iron, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The rod of iron represents the word of God. Those who hearken to the word of God and hold fast to it will not perish or be overcome by the adversary.

l: the word of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The word of God is represented by the rod of iron and protects those who hold fast to it from temptation and destruction. Nephi exhorts his brethren to give heed to it and keep the commandments.

l: the river of water, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The river of water in Nephi's father's dream represents filthiness and an awful gulf separating the wicked from the tree of life and the saints of God.

l: the ball, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The ball is a round object of fine brass containing two spindles that point the way through the wilderness. Its pointers and writing work and change according to the family's faith and diligence, giving them understanding and directions.

l: Nephi's bow, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi's bow is made of fine steel and breaks while he is hunting for food. Its loss contributes to the family's famine, after which Nephi makes a new bow from wood.

l: the gospel of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The fulness of the gospel of the Messiah will come to the Gentiles and then to the remnant of the seed. It enables them to know their Redeemer and the points of his doctrine so they may come unto him and be saved.

l: the covenant with Abraham, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The covenant with Abraham promises that all the kindreds of the earth will be blessed through Abraham's seed. Nephi identifies it as the covenant to be fulfilled in the latter days.

l: the restoration of the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The restoration of the Jews will occur in the latter days. After being restored, the Jews will no more be confounded or scattered again.

l: the scattering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The scattering of Israel occurs through the Gentiles before the natural branches are grafted in and the remnant of the seed is restored among the house of Israel.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The grafting in of the natural branches occurs in the latter days after the seed has dwindled in unbelief and the fulness of the gospel has come through the Gentiles.

l: the three days' journey into the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The journey into the wilderness begins when the Lord commands Nephi's father to depart on the morrow. The family gathers provisions and seed, crosses the river Laman, follows the ball, and travels through the wilderness for many days.

l: Ishmael's death, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Ishmael's death occurs at Nahom during the family's journey in the wilderness. His daughters mourn and then murmur against Nephi's father and Nephi.

l: the judgment of mankind, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: People will be judged according to their works, including the works done by the temporal body during the days of probation. Those who are filthy cannot enter the kingdom of God.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi teaches that knowledge is received through faith, diligence, and keeping the commandments of the Lord. He repeatedly exhorts his brethren to keep them.

l: faith and diligence, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Faith and diligence affect whether the ball's pointers work and what is written upon it. The writing changes according to the faith and diligence given to it.

l: murmuring against the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Murmuring against the Lord occurs after Nephi's bow breaks and the family suffers from hunger. The Lord chastens the murmurers, who turn away their anger and repent.

l: Nephi's preaching, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: Nephi preaches to his brethren about the house of Israel, the restoration of the Jews, the meaning of his father's dream, the judgment of mankind, and the need to keep the commandments.

l: the famine in the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The famine in the wilderness follows the breaking of Nephi's bow and the loss of the other bows' springs. The family suffers hunger until Nephi obtains food by using his new bow.

l: the written directions on the ball, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 15 .. Chapter 16
s: The written directions on the ball give understanding concerning the ways of the Lord and guide the family through the wilderness. The writing is plain to read and changes according to their faith and diligence.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi and his family travel through the wilderness to the land of Bountiful, where the Lord commands Nephi to construct a ship. Nephi makes tools, builds the ship according to the Lord’s instructions, and rebukes his brethren when they murmur against him. During the voyage, Laman, Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and their wives bind Nephi, causing the compass to stop and a great storm to arise. After Nephi is loosed, he prays, the storm ceases, and the family arrives in the promised land, where they plant seeds and find abundant crops, animals, and ore.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi travels with his family through the wilderness and reaches the land of Bountiful. The Lord commands him to construct a ship, and he makes tools, builds the ship according to the Lord’s instructions, guides it to the promised land, and prays for the storm to cease after his brethren bind him.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The Lord nourishes and strengthens Nephi’s family in the wilderness, provides food and light, and leads them toward the promised land. He commands Nephi to build a ship, shows him how to work its timbers, shakes Nephi’s brethren, stops the compass when Nephi is bound, and calms the storm after Nephi prays.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Lehi leads his family from the land of Jerusalem into the wilderness and receives the Lord’s command that they should arise and go down into the ship. He has two sons born in the wilderness, Jacob and Joseph.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Laman murmurs against Nephi and helps bind him with cords during the voyage. When the storm threatens destruction, he repents and helps loose Nephi.

l: Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Lemuel murmurs against Nephi and helps bind him with cords during the voyage. When the storm threatens destruction, he repents and helps loose Nephi.

l: Laman and Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi’s brethren murmur that he cannot build a ship and refuse to believe that he was instructed by the Lord. They are confounded by Nephi’s words, are shaken by the Lord, later bind Nephi during the voyage, and repent when the storm threatens to destroy them.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi’s family travels nearly eastward through the wilderness for eight years, suffering affliction while living upon raw meat. The wilderness provides fruit, wild honey, beasts, and ore, and the family eventually leaves it for the promised land.

l: the land of Bountiful, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The family reaches the land of Bountiful after many years in the wilderness. They call it Bountiful because of its much fruit and wild honey, pitch their tents by the seashore, and begin preparing there to build a ship.

l: the sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The family beholds the sea at Bountiful and calls it Irreantum, meaning many waters. They later cross it in the ship toward the promised land, though a storm drives them back for four days.

l: the promised land, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The family arrives at the promised land after Nephi guides the ship there. They pitch their tents, plant the seeds brought from the land of Jerusalem, receive abundant growth, and find many animals and ores.

l: the ship, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi constructs the ship from timbers according to the manner shown by the Lord rather than the manner of men. The family boards it with provisions, seeds, wives, and children, and it carries them toward the promised land.

l: the compass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The compass, which was prepared by the Lord, ceases to work after Nephi is bound by his brethren. After they loose Nephi, it works again according to his desire.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The commandments of God must be fulfilled, and those who keep them are nourished, strengthened, and provided means to accomplish what God commands. Nephi strives to keep them and exhorts his brethren to faithfulness and diligence.

l: the word of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: Nephi teaches that the children of Israel were led, fed, protected, and delivered by the word and power of God. He also warns his brethren that they have heard the word of God but hardened their hearts and were past feeling.

l: the construction of the ship, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The construction of the ship begins after the Lord commands Nephi to build it and tells him where to find ore. Nephi makes tools, receives repeated instruction from the Lord, and completes workmanship that his brethren recognize as exceedingly fine.

l: the voyage to the promised land, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: The voyage begins after the family boards the ship with provisions, seeds, and their families. Nephi’s brethren bind him, the compass stops, and the ship is driven backward by a great storm until they repent; afterward Nephi guides the ship to the promised land.

l: the great storm, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 17 .. Chapter 18
s: A great and terrible storm arises after Nephi is bound and the compass ceases to work. The ship is driven back for four days, and the storm ends only after Nephi is loosed and prays to the Lord.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi explains that the Lord commanded him to make plates of ore and record his father’s record, their journey in the wilderness, and prophecies. He teaches that the God of Israel will be rejected, scourged, crucified, and buried, while signs and judgments will come upon the house of Israel and Jerusalem. Nephi reads from the plates of brass, including the writings of Isaiah, to teach his people about the Lord and give them hope. The unit also describes the future remembrance of covenants, gathering of Israel, and salvation for all nations, kindreds, tongues, and peoples.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi makes plates of ore by commandment, records sacred things and prophecies, and teaches his people from the plates of brass. He seeks to persuade the house of Israel to remember the Lord their Redeemer and reads Isaiah to his brethren.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The God of Israel is trampled under the feet of men, rejected, scourged, smitten, spat upon, and crucified. He yields himself into the hands of wicked men and will later remember his covenants with the house of Israel.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi records his father’s record, genealogy, journeyings in the wilderness, and prophecies on the first plates.

l: Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi makes records for the instruction of his people and teaches them about the Lord’s dealings and the writings of ancient prophets.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The house of Israel will be visited with joy and salvation or with judgments because of righteousness or rejection of the Holy One of Israel. When its people no longer turn aside their hearts, the Lord will remember his covenants and gather them from the four quarters of the earth.

l: prophets, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Prophets of old were shown things concerning Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and Nephi’s people. Their writings are preserved on the plates of brass.

l: Isaiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Isaiah’s writings are read by Nephi to persuade his brethren to believe in the Lord their Redeemer. Nephi likens Isaiah’s words to his people so they may have hope.

l: plates of ore, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi makes plates of ore by commandment and engraves upon them the record of his people, his father’s record, their journeyings, and prophecies.

l: plates of Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The other plates contain a greater account of the wars, contentions, and destructions of Nephi’s people. They are to be handed down from one generation or prophet to another until further commandments of the Lord.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The plates of brass contain writings about the Lord’s dealings in other lands and among people of old, including the books of Moses and the writings of Isaiah.

l: account of the ministry of Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi engraves the record of his people on the plates of ore, including his father’s record, their journeyings in the wilderness, and many of his own prophecies.

l: scriptures, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi likens all scriptures unto his people for their profit and learning. He reads from the scriptures to persuade them to believe in the Lord their Redeemer.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Those at Jerusalem will scourge and be scourged by all people because they crucify the God of Israel and reject signs, wonders, power, and glory. They will wander in the flesh, perish, and become a hiss and a byword among nations.

l: wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The wilderness is the setting of the journey of Nephi’s family, and the first plates contain much of their proceedings there.

l: the isles of the sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The isles of the sea will receive signs of the God of Israel’s death through three days of darkness. The Lord will remember the isles of the sea and gather the house of Israel.

l: prophecies, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi engraves many of his own prophecies and records the prophecies of his father. The prophecies concern the ministry, suffering, death, resurrection-related signs, judgments, covenants, and gathering of Israel.

l: wars, contentions, and destructions, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The other plates give a greater account of the wars, contentions, and destructions of Nephi’s people.

l: the land of promise journey, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi records the journeyings of his family in the wilderness on the plates of ore and the first plates.

l: making of the plates, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Nephi makes the plates by commandment of the Lord so that sacred things may be preserved for the knowledge and instruction of his people.

l: crucifixion of Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The God of Israel will be crucified according to the words of Neum, and those at Jerusalem will be judged because they crucify him.

l: three days of darkness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: Three days of darkness will be a sign of the God of Israel’s death, especially for those who inhabit the isles of the sea and those of the house of Israel.

l: salvation, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The righteous among the house of Israel will receive great joy and salvation when the Lord visits them. All the earth will see the salvation of the Lord, and every nation, kindred, tongue, and people will be blessed.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: When the house of Israel no longer turns aside its heart against the Holy One of Israel, the Lord will remember the covenants he made with its fathers.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 19
s: The Lord will gather all people of the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth, including those on the isles of the sea.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: The Lord addresses the house of Jacob, who are called Israel and come forth from the waters of Judah or baptism, but who swear by the Lord without truth or righteousness. The Lord explains that he declared former and hidden things because the house of Jacob was obstinate and treacherous, and he refined it in the furnace of affliction for his own name’s sake. The Lord promises to fulfill his word against Babylon and the Chaldeans, and calls Jacob to leave Babylon and declare that the Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob. The Lord says that peace would have been like a river if Jacob had hearkened to his commandments, but there is no peace to the wicked.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: The house of Jacob is called by the name of Israel and comes forth out of the waters of Judah or baptism. It swears by the name of the Lord and makes mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth or righteousness; it is described as obstinate, treacherous, and a transgressor from the womb.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: The Lord declares former and hidden things, refines the house of Jacob in the furnace of affliction, and defers his anger for his own name’s sake. He lays the foundation of the earth, spans the heavens, teaches and leads, promises to fulfill his word against Babylon and the Chaldeans, and redeems his servant Jacob.

l: affliction, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: Affliction is described as a furnace in which the Lord has refined and chosen the house of Jacob.

l: Babylon, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: Babylon is the place from which Jacob is commanded to go forth and flee. The Lord will do his pleasure on Babylon.

l: Chaldeans, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: The Chaldeans are commanded to be fled from, and the Lord's arm shall come upon them.

l: peace, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 20
s: Peace would have been like a river if the house of Jacob had hearkened to the Lord's commandments. There is no peace, saith the Lord, unto the wicked.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The Lord addresses the house of Israel, including those broken off and scattered because of the wickedness of the pastors of the people. He describes his servant as a light to the Gentiles and as a means of salvation unto the ends of the earth, and promises to restore Israel, comfort the afflicted, and gather its people from far places. Zion is assured that the Lord has not forgotten her, will protect her children, and will cause kings and queens to support her. The Lord declares that he will deliver the captives, save the children of Israel, and make all flesh know that he is their Savior and Redeemer.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The house of Israel includes those who are broken off and scattered because of the wickedness of the pastors of the people. The Lord promises not to forget it, to gather its children, and to deliver and save them.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The Lord calls and prepares his servant, promises to be his strength, and gives him for a light to the Gentiles. The Lord comforts his people, preserves them, gathers them, contends with their oppressors, and saves their children.

l: Zion, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: Zion says that the Lord has forsaken and forgotten her, but the Lord declares that he has not forgotten her. He promises that her children will return, that her desolate places will be filled, and that kings and queens will honor and support her.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The Gentiles are given the servant of the Lord as a light and as salvation unto the ends of the earth. The Lord will lift up his hand to them and cause them to bring the children of Israel back.

l: servant of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The servant of the Lord is called from the womb, made a sharp sword and a polished shaft, and hidden in the Lord's hand and quiver. He is appointed to bring Jacob back, restore Israel, serve as a light to the Gentiles, and be given as a covenant of the people.

l: covenant, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The Lord gives his servant as a covenant of the people. This covenant is connected with establishing the earth and causing the desolate heritages to be inherited.

l: salvation, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The servant is given as a light to the Gentiles so that he may be the Lord's salvation unto the ends of the earth. The Lord also speaks of a day of salvation in which he helps and preserves.

l: redemption, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: The Lord identifies himself as the Redeemer of Israel and declares that he will deliver the captives and the prey of the terrible. He will contend with those who contend with his people and save their children.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 21
s: Israel is described as broken off, driven out, and scattered abroad because of the wickedness of the pastors of the people. Its restoration includes being gathered from far places, returning to Zion, inheriting desolate places, and being delivered from oppressors.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Nephi explains to his brethren that the plates of brass concern the temporal and spiritual scattering and gathering of the house of Israel. He teaches that the Lord God will raise up a nation among the Gentiles, perform a marvelous work, reveal his covenants and gospel, and gather Israel. The wicked, the great and abominable church, and all who fight against Zion will be brought down, while the righteous will be preserved. Nephi concludes that the writings testify that people must obey the commandments of God and endure to the end to be saved at the last day.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Nephi explains the prophecies on the plates of brass to his brethren. He teaches about the scattering and gathering of Israel, the destruction of the wicked, and the preservation and salvation of the righteous.

l: Laman and Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Nephi's brethren ask what the things on the plates of brass mean. They are taught that the prophecies concern both spiritual and temporal things.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The house of Israel will be scattered among all nations and hated because of the Holy One of Israel. It will later be gathered to the lands of its inheritance and learn that the Lord is its Savior and Redeemer.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Gentiles will nurse and carry the seed of Israel, and the Lord God will raise up a mighty nation among them. They will receive a marvelous work that is also of worth to them.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Lord God will raise up a mighty nation among the Gentiles, make bare his arm, bring about his covenants and gospel, and gather Israel. He will preserve the righteous and destroy those who fight against Zion.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Holy One of Israel is the prophet spoken of by Moses and will execute judgment in righteousness. He will reign in dominion, might, power, and great glory, and will feed his gathered sheep.

l: Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Jesus Christ is not named in this unit.

l: Satan, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Satan will have no more power over the hearts of the children of men during the righteous reign. He cannot be loosed for many years because of the righteousness of the people.

l: the great and abominable church, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The great and abominable church will turn upon its own head, tumble to the dust, and suffer a great fall. It is described as having perverted the right ways of the Lord.

l: the kingdom of the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The kingdom of the devil is built up among the children of men in the flesh. Those belonging to it will be brought low and consumed as stubble.

l: the righteous, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The righteous need not fear because they will be preserved, even through the destruction of their enemies by fire. They will dwell safely if they repent and will be led up as calves of the stall.

l: the children of men, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The children of men will experience the consequences of hardening their hearts against the Holy One of Israel. Satan will lose power over their hearts when the people dwell in righteousness.

l: remnant of the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Nephi's seed will be scattered by the mighty nation raised up among the Gentiles. The marvelous work among the Gentiles will be of great worth to them.

l: the nations, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The nations will see the Lord God make bare his arm in bringing about his covenants and gospel. Nations that war against the house of Israel will be turned against one another and fall into the pit they dig.

l: the land of inheritance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: This land is the place where the Lord God will raise up a mighty nation among the Gentiles. Blood, fire, and vapor of smoke must come upon its face if people harden their hearts.

l: Zion, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: All who fight against Zion will be destroyed.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The plates of brass contain writings that testify that the prophecies are true and that people must be obedient to the commandments of God.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The covenants of the Lord with the fathers concern the scattering and later gathering of the house of Israel. They include the promise to Abraham that all the kindreds of the earth will be blessed through his seed.

l: the gospel of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Lord God will bring his gospel to those who are of the house of Israel as part of making bare his arm among the nations.

l: obedience to the commandments of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Obedience to the commandments of God is required for salvation at the last day, together with enduring to the end.

l: the scattering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The scattering of Israel will occur among all the nations and across the earth. It will happen because many harden their hearts against the Holy One of Israel.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The gathering of Israel will bring the people out of captivity, obscurity, and darkness to the lands of their inheritance. They will know the Lord as their Savior and Redeemer.

l: the marvelous work among the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Lord God will perform a marvelous work among the Gentiles after Nephi's seed is scattered. It will nourish Israel and be of great worth to both Israel and the Gentiles.

l: the destruction of the wicked, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The wicked will be brought low, consumed as stubble, and destroyed. The righteous will be preserved while the enemies of the Lord are destroyed by fire.

l: the reign of the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The Holy One of Israel will reign in dominion, might, power, and great glory. During his reign, the gathered people will form one fold with one shepherd.

l: the millennium of righteousness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: The millennium of righteousness is not named in this unit.

l: the last day, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 22
s: Those who are obedient to the commandments of God and endure to the end will be saved at the last day.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi teaches his sons about the Lord’s mercy in bringing them from Jerusalem to the land of promise and warns that obedience will bring liberty and prosperity, while iniquity will bring judgments, scattering, and captivity. He urges Laman, Lemuel, Sam, the sons of Ishmael, and Zoram to obey Nephi, cease rebelling, and unite in righteousness. Lehi testifies that the Lord has redeemed him and that he will soon die, and he gives blessings and promises concerning the seed of Zoram and Nephi.

l: Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi teaches his sons about the Lord’s dealings, the land of promise, obedience, rebellion, and the consequences of iniquity. Near death, he urges them to obey Nephi, unite in righteousness, and remember the Lord’s commandments; he also gives blessings to Laman, Lemuel, Sam, the sons of Ishmael, and Zoram.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Nephi has taught his brethren and is described by Lehi as having kept the commandments, brought the family through the wilderness, and sought the glory of God and their eternal welfare. Lehi commands his brethren to cease rebelling against him and says that blessings will rest upon Nephi if they will not hearken to him.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The Lord God warns Lehi’s family to flee Jerusalem, brings people to the land of promise, and covenants concerning the land. He blesses those who keep his commandments and brings judgments, other nations, scattering, and captivity upon those who reject him.

l: Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jerusalem is the land from which Lehi’s family was warned to flee. Lehi says he saw that Jerusalem was destroyed and that his family would have perished if they had remained there.

l: land of promise, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The land of promise is described as choice above all other lands and consecrated for those whom the Lord brings there. It will be a land of liberty, prosperity, security, and inheritance for the righteous, but iniquity will cause it to be cursed and its people to be removed from their possessions.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Other nations are to be kept from the land of promise while the people brought from Jerusalem keep the Lord’s commandments. If they reject the Holy One of Israel, the Lord will bring other nations against them and give those nations power over them.

l: seed of Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The seed of Lehi is promised an inheritance in the land of promise. If they keep the Lord’s commandments, they will prosper, possess the land, and dwell safely; if they reject the Lord, they will face judgments, scattering, and loss of their lands.

l: vision of Jerusalem's destruction, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi says that he saw a vision in which he knew that Jerusalem was destroyed. The vision confirmed that remaining in Jerusalem would have caused his family to perish.

l: departure from Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The departure from Jerusalem occurred because the Lord warned Lehi’s family to flee. Lehi teaches that the Lord brought them into the land of promise and that their preservation came through this departure.

l: rebellion, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi recalls his sons’ rebellions on the waters and says that God spared their lives. He commands them to rebel no more against Nephi, whom they had sought to kill despite his service and faithfulness.

l: covenant concerning the land, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The Lord covenants with Lehi that the land will be an inheritance for his seed, his children, and those led there by the Lord. The covenant promises liberty, prosperity, protection, and possession of the land to those who keep the Lord’s commandments.

l: commandments, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi urges his sons to remember and observe the commandments, statutes, and judgments of the Lord. Keeping them brings prosperity, blessing, liberty, security, and protection from captivity.

l: law of prosperity and destruction, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The law states that those who keep the Lord’s commandments will prosper in the land, while those who refuse will be cut off from his presence. Continued iniquity can bring cursing, destruction of soul and body, loss of possessions, scattering, and captivity.

l: iniquity, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Iniquity causes the land to be cursed and brings the Lord’s wrath, judgments, sword, famine, hatred, captivity, and destruction. Lehi fears that the hardness of his sons’ hearts will bring these consequences upon them.

l: judgments of God, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The judgments of God rest upon those who reject the Holy One of Israel after receiving great blessings and knowledge. These judgments include the arrival of other nations, loss of lands, scattering, smiting, bloodshed, and great visitations.

l: scattering and captivity, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Scattering and captivity are consequences of rejecting the Lord and failing to keep his commandments. Lehi warns that the people may lose their lands, be scattered and smitten, and be led according to the will and captivity of the devil.

l: death of Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi says that he will soon lay down his limbs in the cold and silent grave and go the way of all the earth. Before his death, he urges his sons to arise, obey, unite, and avoid bringing him grief and sorrow.

l: the power of God, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The power of God is said to be with Nephi, enabling him to command his brethren to obey. Lehi explains that it was the Spirit of the Lord in Nephi that opened his mouth and caused him to speak boldly.

l: chains of sin, The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Lehi calls on his sons to awake from the sleep of hell and shake off the awful chains that bind the children of men. He identifies these chains with captivity and misery and urges them to put on the armor of righteousness and arise from the dust.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Lehi teaches Jacob and his sons that God created all things and that opposition, law, and choice are necessary to fulfill God's eternal purposes. He explains that Adam and Eve's transgression brought the fall of man, mortality, probation, and knowledge of good and evil, while Adam's fall made it possible for men to exist and have joy. The Holy Messiah provides redemption and salvation through his merits, mercy, grace, sacrifice, intercession, and resurrection. Men are free to choose liberty and eternal life through the great Mediator or captivity and eternal death through the devil.

l: Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Jacob is Lehi's first-born in the wilderness and suffered afflictions and sorrow because of his brethren. He knows the greatness of God, will dwell safely with Nephi, and is redeemed through the righteousness of his Redeemer.

l: Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Lehi teaches Jacob and his sons about God, creation, opposition, the fall, redemption, and the choices before men. He says he has chosen the good part and seeks the everlasting welfare of their souls.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: God created the heavens, the earth, and all things in them, including things to act and things to be acted upon. God gave commandments, established law, and has eternal purposes involving man's probation, agency, judgment, and redemption.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The Holy Messiah is full of grace and truth and offers himself as a sacrifice for sin for those with a broken heart and contrite spirit. He lays down his life according to the flesh, takes it again by the power of the Spirit, brings the resurrection of the dead, and makes intercession for all the children of men.

l: Adam, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Adam transgressed, fell from the garden of Eden, and thereby made it possible for men to be. Through his fall, mankind entered a state of probation and became able to know good from evil and have joy.

l: Eve, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Eve was told by the old serpent to partake of the forbidden fruit and become as God, knowing good and evil. After she and Adam partook, they were driven out of the garden of Eden to till the earth.

l: the devil, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The devil was an angel who fell from heaven after seeking evil before God. He seeks the misery of all mankind and uses captivity and his power to bring men down to hell.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Men are instructed sufficiently to know good from evil and are subject to law, judgment, and the consequences of their choices. They may choose liberty and eternal life through the great Mediator or captivity and death through the devil.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The earth was created by God along with the heavens and all things in them. It would not have existed if there were no God or creation.

l: the garden of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The garden of Eden was where Adam and Eve would have remained if Adam had not transgressed. After partaking of the forbidden fruit, they were driven out to till the earth.

l: the resurrection, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The resurrection of the dead is brought to pass by the Holy Messiah, who lays down his life and takes it again by the power of the Spirit. He is the first that should rise.

l: fall of man, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The fall of man came through Adam and Eve's transgression and brought mankind out of the garden of Eden. Through the Messiah, the children of men are redeemed from the fall and become free to act for themselves.

l: transgression of Adam, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Adam's transgression caused him to fall and prevented mankind from remaining forever in a state of innocence. It made possible the existence of men, their probation, and their opportunity to have joy.

l: forbidden fruit, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The forbidden fruit stood in opposition to the tree of life. After Adam and Eve partook of it, they were driven out of the garden of Eden and came to know good and evil.

l: law, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The law is given to men so that they know good from evil, but no flesh is justified by the law. The law cuts men off and affixes punishment, while the Messiah answers its ends for those with a broken heart and contrite spirit.

l: sin, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Sin exists because there is law and opposition. Without sin there would be no righteousness, happiness, punishment, or misery.

l: righteousness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Righteousness is possible because there is law and opposition. Those who believe in the Messiah may be saved through his intercession and righteousness.

l: good and evil, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Men are instructed sufficiently to know good from evil. The fall and redemption leave men free to act for themselves while knowing good from evil.

l: salvation, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Salvation is free and is prepared from the fall of man. No flesh can dwell in God's presence except through the merits, mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah.

l: redemption, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Redemption comes through the Holy Messiah, who offers himself as a sacrifice for sin and makes intercession for mankind. The children of men are redeemed from the fall through him.

l: the atonement, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The atonement answers the ends of the law and is connected with the punishment and happiness affixed to men's choices. Its benefits are received through the Holy Messiah.

l: opposition, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Opposition is necessary in all things so that righteousness, wickedness, holiness, misery, good, and bad can exist. It existed between the forbidden fruit and the tree of life and enables meaningful choice.

l: agency, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Men are given the ability to act for themselves rather than merely be acted upon. They are enticed by one choice or the other and may choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death.

l: liberty, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Liberty is available to men through the great Mediator of all men. Choosing liberty leads toward eternal life.

l: captivity, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Captivity is associated with the power and will of the devil. Choosing captivity leads to death and gives the devil power to bring men down to hell.

l: eternal life, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Men may choose eternal life through the great Mediator and according to the will of the Holy Spirit. They are instructed to look to the Mediator, hearken to his commandments, and be faithful to his words.

l: everlasting death, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Men may choose eternal death according to the will of the flesh and the evil within it. This choice gives the spirit of the devil power to captivate them and bring them down to hell.

l: happiness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Happiness is opposed to punishment and misery and depends on righteousness. Adam's fall made it possible for men to have joy, and the absence of righteousness would mean the absence of happiness.

l: misery, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Misery is opposed to happiness and is associated with wickedness, punishment, and the devil's purposes. The devil seeks that all mankind might be miserable like himself.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Lehi blesses Joseph, his last-born son, and teaches that Joseph's seed will not be destroyed if they keep the commandments of the Holy One of Israel. Joseph prophesied that the Lord would raise up a choice seer from his loins to bring forth the word of the Lord, write records, and help convince his descendants of the Lord's word. The writings of Joseph's descendants and Judah's descendants will grow together to confound false doctrines, lay down contentions, establish peace, and bring the descendants to knowledge of their fathers and the covenants of the Lord. The unit also describes the Messiah, Moses, a spokesman, one mighty among Joseph's descendants, and the future restoration of the house of Israel.

l: Joseph (Lehi's last-born son), The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Joseph is Lehi's last-born son, born in the wilderness during Lehi's greatest sorrow. Lehi blesses him with the land of inheritance and teaches him about his lineage, the choice seer, and the promises concerning his seed.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Joseph is instructed to hearken unto the words of his brother, Nephi.

l: Moses, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Moses is the one whom the Lord will raise up to deliver the people of Israel from Egypt. The Lord will give him power in a rod, judgment in writing, and a spokesman, but will not loose his tongue to speak much.

l: the Messiah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Messiah is to be made manifest to the branch of Israel in the latter days, bringing them out of darkness and captivity unto light and freedom.

l: the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Lord makes covenants and promises concerning Joseph's seed, raises up a choice seer and Moses, gives commandments and power, preserves Joseph's seed, and brings about salvation and restoration.

l: Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Holy One of Israel gives commandments whose observance is tied to Joseph's inheritance and the preservation of his seed.

l: Joseph's brethren, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Joseph's brethren are the fruit of Joseph's loins, and the choice seer will do a work of great worth for them by bringing them to knowledge of the covenants.

l: house of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The house of Israel will be delivered, restored, and brought to knowledge of the covenants. The Messiah will be made manifest to it in the latter days.

l: the fruit of Joseph's loins, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The fruit of Joseph's loins will produce written words, receive the work of a choice seer, and be preserved because of the covenant. Its words will come together with the writings of Judah's descendants and will cry from the dust to later generations.

l: the fruit of Judah's loins, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The fruit of Judah's loins will write, and its writing will grow together with the writing of Joseph's descendants to confound false doctrines, lay down contentions, and establish peace.

l: a choice seer, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: A choice seer will be raised up from the fruit of Joseph's loins and esteemed highly among them. He will receive commandments and power to bring forth and convince Joseph's descendants of the word of the Lord, and his work will help bring them to salvation.

l: the spokesman, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The spokesman will be made for the one raised up from Joseph's loins and will declare the writing produced by Joseph's descendants.

l: one mighty among them, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: One mighty among Joseph's descendants will do much good in word and deed as an instrument in the hands of God, work mighty wonders, and bring much restoration to the house of Israel and Joseph's brethren.

l: lands of promise, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The land of inheritance is described as a most precious land that the Lord may consecrate to Joseph and his seed for their security forever if they keep the commandments.

l: the latter days, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: In the latter days, the Messiah will be made manifest, Joseph's descendants will be brought to knowledge of their fathers and the covenants, and the house of Israel will be restored.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The covenants of the Lord include promises concerning Joseph's lineage, the choice seer, the preservation of Joseph's seed, and the restoration and knowledge of Israel.

l: the promise of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The promise of the Lord is that a righteous branch will come from Joseph's loins, that a choice seer will be raised up, and that Joseph's seed will be preserved and not destroyed.

l: word of the Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The word of the Lord will be brought forth by the choice seer and will be used to convince Joseph's descendants. The writings of Joseph's descendants will also be the words expedient in the Lord's wisdom.

l: the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The book will be heeded by Joseph's seed, helping ensure that they are not destroyed. Its words will be as if Joseph's descendants cried to later generations from the dust.

l: darkness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Messiah will bring Joseph's branch out of hidden darkness and the house of Israel out of darkness unto light.

l: captivity, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Messiah will bring Joseph's branch out of captivity unto freedom.

l: freedom, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Freedom is part of the deliverance the Messiah will bring to Joseph's branch from captivity.

l: salvation, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The work brought forth by the promised seer will bring Joseph's people unto salvation through the power of the Lord.

l: restoration of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: One mighty among Joseph's descendants will work much restoration unto the house of Israel and the seed of Joseph's brethren.
